# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 46 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 46 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_046_page_001.jpg

---

## Council Notes

This chapter presents Hermas's soteriology in its most concentrated form. Three categories emerge: (1) the pure-hearted who keep the commandments and live; (2) the well-intentioned but weak who stumble — they are forgiven and saved through the Angel of Righteousness; (3) the forgetful and impenitent who are handed to the Angel of Punishment.

The Angel of Punishment (*angelos timōrias*) here is corrective, not eschatologically final — a purgatorial figure. This is remarkable for a 2nd-century text. The purpose of his chastisement is explicitly "*eis sōtērian*" — for/toward salvation.

The catalog of divine attributes in 46:5 — philanthropy, gentleness, forbearance, mercy — reflects a standard Hellenistic-Jewish-Christian virtue list for God's character. *Philanthropia* (love of humanity) is a particularly Greek theological term.

EMET renders *philanthropia* as "love of humanity"; LOGOS similarly; PNEUMA as "love for humanity." SOPHIA uses "philanthropy" as a transliteration — it is a Greek theological term worth preserving in a scholarly translation.

---

## Mandate 12, Part 3 — The Angel of Righteousness and the Angel of Punishment

**46:1** I said to him: "Lord, now that I have come to the end of these commandments, I ask whether a man is able to keep them, given how great and demanding they are." "You shall keep them," he said, "if your heart is pure toward God. And all who have purified their hearts from the empty desires of this age shall keep them and shall live to God."

**46:2** "Lord," I said, "now that I have heard these commandments: if any man is unable to keep them because of the weakness of the flesh, what will become of him?" "If he undertakes to keep them but does not, and his heart is turned away from the Lord, he shall die. But he who undertakes them with his whole heart and labors to do what is right, even if he stumbles at times on account of the weakness of the flesh — this man shall live, because the Lord is compassionate."

**46:3** "The Lord sees that his heart is pure and has compassion on that man and forgives him all his transgressions. He strengthens the man and grants him to keep the commandments of the Angel of Righteousness, and so grants him salvation."

**46:4** "But for the man who lives in forgetfulness and does not keep the commandments of the Lord, the Lord hands him over to the angel of punishment, and that angel chastises him for his wickedness unto salvation."

**46:5** "But Lord," I said, "how can the Lord be simultaneously so compassionate and yet permit such chastisement?" "Listen," he said. "The Lord is compassionate in all his works and all his words. He is full of philanthropy and gentleness and forbearance and mercy. Therefore so long as a man repents, he has hope. But when he turns away from God and sins without repentance, there is no hope for him."

---

*SOPHIA represents the consensus rendering of EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA, with rulings recorded in the Disagreement Log.*
